name: Baoulé
notes: Standard Baoulé Latin orthography codified in 1979 by the Institut de Linguistique Appliquée (ILA, Abidjan; alphabet chart cited via Omniglot). 28-letter alphabet A B C D E Ɛ F G GB I J L K KP M N NY O Ɔ P S T U V W Y Z; the seven oral vowels /a e ɛ i o ɔ u/ contrast with five nasal counterparts /ã ɛ̃ ĩ ɔ̃ ũ/ written with a combining tilde, each spelling one nasalized nucleus rather than an oral vowel plus a separate nasal segment (AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨gb⟩ and ⟨kp⟩ are the single labial-velar stops /ɡb/ and /kp/ (test 1: g+b would give /ɡb/ as a cluster, not the coarticulated stop the language actually has, so the digraph earns its key on the phonological-unit test, test 2). ⟨ny⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/, distinct from the nasal-assimilation allophone [ɲ] that /m/ and /n/ (and the /ɟ/ allophone series inherited from the prior stub) already carry before a following palatal. ⟨c⟩ and ⟨j⟩ are the voiceless/voiced palatal stops /c/ and /ɟ/ (not the affricates /tʃ dʒ/); the palatal glide is spelled ⟨y⟩ /j/. Smoke-tested against the Universal Declaration of Human Rights Art. 1 Baoulé translation (Omniglot): ⟨Sran⟩ [sran] 'person', ⟨be⟩ [be] 'they', ⟨ngba⟩ [ŋɡba] 'all', ⟨kε⟩ [kɛ] 'that', ⟨wu⟩ [wu] 'die/kill', ⟨fɔndi⟩ [fɔⁿdi] 'freedom' — each renders with the mapped graphemes above; ⟨fɔndi⟩'s medial ⟨nd⟩ is a nasal-assimilation surface form of /n/+/d/, not a distinct grapheme. Baoulé is a five-tone Kwa language (high, low, mid, rising, falling; Timyan 1977) with no lexical word stress; tone is not consistently marked in everyday orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
